Yeah. I'm not really a fan, either. I feel like it falls way too far short of what it's cracked up to be. Granted, I haven't been keeping up with the site, so I don't know what's going on over there anymore. All I can say is that I don't think the invite system is working in their favor.

Invite systems work wonders for private torrent trackers which have a lot to lose if the wrong kinda person gets access. Some trackers even require interviews for prospective members. I don't think that's viable for a site like this but it does segue into the idea that making users jump through some hoops keeps out the image-macro puking riffraff. Hell, back in the day just getting the hardware to get online was hard enough. The net communities formed during the early internet weren't just small because of the money needed to hook up, they were made of amazingly smart people because you had to have at least some brains to get in the door.

One thing I've love to see is the split of users-with-accounts versus total users on reddit. With news aggregators, it's not that bad to be signed-out. Sites like digg, reddit, voat still work in read-only mode and it may be better if the number of active contributors is artificially kept somewhat small.

It's actually really hard to make a website popular. It doesn't happen by accident. Worrying about it happening against your will is like the people who are afraid to lift weights because they don't want to look like a body builder. It's just not something that will happen without relentless effort.
